definition: Artificial intelligence engineering (AI engineering) is a technical discipline that focuses on the design, development, and deployment of AI systems.
details: AI engineering involves applying engineering principles and methodologies to create scalable, efficient, and reliable AI-based solutions. It merges aspects of data engineering and software engineering to create real-world applications in diverse domains such as healthcare, finance, autonomous systems, and industrial automation.

explainer.lead: AI engineering turns AI techniques into systems people can use in real-world settings. It matters because those systems must be scalable, efficient, and reliable, not merely functional in isolation.

tiers.eli5: Building an AI system is like building a dependable robot helper, not just teaching it one trick. Its information must be organized, its software parts must work together, and the whole system must keep working well when people use it.
tiers.practitioner: In practice, AI engineers combine data-engineering work with software-engineering methods to design, build, and deploy AI-based applications. Typical settings include healthcare, finance, autonomous systems, and industrial automation. Common pitfalls are treating model development as the whole job or overlooking scalability, efficiency, and reliability during deployment.
tiers.paperLevel: AI engineering is the technical discipline concerned with the design, development, and deployment of AI systems, using engineering principles and methodologies to achieve scalability, efficiency, and reliability. Its scope combines aspects of data engineering and software engineering for real-world applications.

explainer.example: A factory wants an AI-based automation system. Engineers organize its data, build the software around the AI component, and deploy the integrated system so it can operate scalably, efficiently, and reliably.

explainer.intuition: An AI capability becomes a useful application only when its data, software, and deployment are engineered as one system. AI engineering supplies the principles and methods for making that system work at real-world scale.
howItWorks: Define the real-world application and its engineering needs.
Prepare and manage data using data-engineering practices.
Build and integrate the AI solution with software-engineering methods.
Deploy the system with attention to scale, efficiency, and reliability.
explainer.whyItMatters: It bridges the gap between AI techniques and dependable applications. This makes AI practical across domains such as healthcare, finance, autonomous systems, and industrial automation.
misconceptions: AI engineering is not just creating an AI model; it covers system design, development, and deployment.
It does not replace data or software engineering; it combines aspects of both.
